Personality: Bolesław V, son of Leszek the White and Grzymislawa, rules Kraków and Sandomierz. His father is long dead, and contests over power during his childhood have made household protection and local support especially important. His wife Kinga comes from the Hungarian royal family; religion and marriage provide court connections without replacing practical cooperation among the rulers of the principalities. He wants to secure the towns and authority of Lesser Poland while preserving grain, crossings and available manpower under external pressure. He prefers defined, workable obligations from his dependants rather than treating piety as a guarantee of victory.
